walkthroughs.body_html:
Wave Phenomena — a core area of Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Wave Phenomena brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Wave Phenomena.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: No — it was the expansion of space itself, beginning from a hot dense state; there was no 'outside' for matter to expand into.

mcqs.q: Why is gravitational potential energy near a planet treated as negative?
options: Gravitational potential energy is negative because gravity does negative work.
Gravitational potential energy is negative because gravity always points downwards.
The temperature at which a substance melts or boils.
Because the zero is defined at infinity; objects bound to the planet have lower (negative) potential energy than at infinity.
